articles.title: Valve 'Thinking About How to Solve' Steam's AI Slop Problem, but Won't Limit Developer Access
articles.summary: Valve’s Steam Business Team took to the stage at the Steam Indie Connect event in Korea and took questions from an audience of game developers. During the chat, the issue of Steam being flooded with generative AI slop games and knockoff AI clones came up, and Valve said it’s still trying to figure out how to navigate this new world.
articles.body:
Valve’s Steam Business Team took to the stage at the Steam Indie Connect event in Korea and took questions from an audience of game developers. During the chat, the issue of Steam being flooded with generative AI slop games and knockoff AI clones came up, and Valve said it’s still trying to figure out how to navigate this new world.

Last year, roughly 17% of Steam Next Fest demos disclosed the use of generative AI, and this year was likely higher as the platform hosted over 8,000 demos during the event. It’s a huge discoverability problem for developers who’ve poured years of their lives into their games, only to get swept up in the slop deluge.

Then there are the AI clones , which are becoming a growing issue. Developers are becoming more and more concerned about showing off their games, as bad actors are using generative AI to clone them from early footage and demos, beating them to the market with a bad copy.

During Steam Indie Connect, Valve’s Tom Giardino addressed concerns around clones, noting that they existed before AI and have only accelerated the process. "We don't want to be gatekeepers telling developers which tools they should or shouldn't use," he said (thanks, InvaGlobal ), ruling out Valve outright banning developers who do this.

"Rather than relying on a single mechanic that someone can easily copy, you need to keep growing your game by adding features, personality, and creativity that stem from your own perspective," he added, shifting the onus onto the developer of the original game.

The issue of discoverability also came up, with developers in the audience noting that it’s harder than ever to stand out among all the throwaway AI games flooding digital storefronts like Steam, but particularly during Next Fest where developers are looking to find their audience ahead of release. According to Valve’s Marc Wilkinson, it’s not as bad as it seems.

During the first two days of Next Fest, recommendations are completely random, but personalized recommendations kick in later based on user activity. Once that kicks in, players are more likely to find the games they love. Wilkinson said that articles pointing out the flood of low-quality games were based on the first couple of days, before personalized recommendations kicked in.

According to Valve, the algorithm has to be completely random at first. This is to prevent system abuse from developers figuring out how to game the algorithm.

"We recognize that the trade-off is that some low-quality games get exposed," Wilkinson said. "We are fully aware of the situation, and a significant number of people are thinking about how to solve this problem."

Giardino added, "We don't think we're perfect and there's plenty of room for improvement. Rather than limiting developer access, making Steam a smarter and more dynamic platform is the starting point of our philosophy."

articles.title: How Does LEGO PlayStation Compare to the Actual Console?
articles.summary: See LEGO PlayStation and Sony's original console side-by-side to see how the LEGO version stacks up to the real thing.
articles.body:
I’m a nostalgic gamer who likes building LEGO sets, which makes me the exact target audience for the LEGO PlayStation set released earlier this month. I built LEGO PlayStation (and enjoyed the whole process from start to finish), but it got me thinking. Since LEGO is billing this as a “near 1:1 scale” recreation of the original hardware, what if I dug out my old PlayStation and compared the two? So that’s exactly what I did.

It turns out, the LEGO designers really did make a near one-to-one recreation of the original hardware, at least on the outside (check out my interview with one of the designers ). The dimensions are almost identical on all sides of the machine. The LEGO version stands slightly taller than the original, but it’s not really noticeable unless you squat down to look at them from the side.

The front of the LEGO set is particularly impressive, with its memory card slots and controller ports. Just like with the real thing, you can plug the LEGO controller into the port on the LEGO console. The main difference is that the LEGO controller’s cord is shorter than the real thing – but that’s what you’d want in a non-functional display set, anyway.

Even the buttons on the console are similar. Pressing the Power button on the real PlayStation turns it on, illuminating a green light below the button. Pressing the same button on the LEGO version raises a translucent green LEGO piece into the same position where the light would be. The Open button is even more impressive. Pressing it on the original hardware opens the PlayStation’s lid so you can put in or remove a game disc. Pressing the same button on the LEGO set also opens the lid.

The main surface-level difference between the LEGO version of the PS1 and the real thing is the selection of ports on the back. The LEGO PlayStation lacks the red, white, and yellow RCA ports. I'm not sure why these were omitted – maybe there were no existing LEGO pieces that could suitably replicate them? But the LEGO set does have ports for Serial I/O, AV Multi Out, and AC In.

I no longer have the original PlayStation controller that came with my console. However, I still have a DualShock controller, which came out in 1997 and made controlling characters in 3D worlds much more intuitive than using a standard D-pad. The DualShock is roughly the same size as the original controller, but it features two analog sticks. The LEGO controller looks pretty similar, but is noticeably more blocky. Still, it’s a fine effort.

One of the biggest things that makes the LEGO PlayStation look similar to the original is that all of the logos and text that appear on the exterior of the console and controller are printed onto the LEGO pieces. They’re not stickers, which I would inevitably have put on slightly askew, making the whole thing look more amateurish. I’m glad they went that route.

As for the other differences? Opening the lid on the LEGO version doesn’t reveal a boring disc drive. It reveals miniature dioramas for 1997’s Gran Turismo and 1999’s Ape Escape. These are little self-contained worlds you can slide out of the set to display next to it, if you’d like. It’s a pretty cool little Easter egg for fans of those games.

LEGO PlayStation vs. the Original Console

Overall, I’m pretty blown away by how similar LEGO PlayStation is to the real thing. Turns out those LEGO designers really know what they’re doing.

Chris Reed is a senior commerce editor and deals expert for IGN. He also runs IGN's LEGO coverage and maintains the upcoming release dates articles for video games , LEGO sets , and 4K Blu-rays . You can follow him on Bluesky .

articles.title: With The Division 3 Still in Active Development, Ubisoft Announces The Division Franchise Has Hit More Than 50 Million Players
articles.summary: Massive Entertainment has announced that The Division series has recorded over 50 million players across its games, just as the series hits its 10th anniversary. That’s a lot of +1 defense beanies!
articles.body:
Massive Entertainment has announced that The Division series has recorded over 50 million players across its games, just as the series hits its 10th anniversary. That’s a lot of +1 defense beanies!

The long-running looter shooter began life in 2016 with the launch of The Division. It came out three years after its flashy reveal at Ubisoft's E3 2013 conference which, at the time, exceeded expectation for next-gen gaming (remember when the guy closed the car door while in cover?). The Division 2 followed in 2019, but sales failed to meet Ubisoft's expectations. A number of spinoffs have come and gone since.

Massive Entertainment announced a new DLC for The Division 2 at a community panel at Gamescom earlier this year. The Echoes of Central Park DLC releases on November 3. It seems likely the new expansion — which adds a horror-themed flashback campaign, a stash space increase, a level boost, and more — will see even more players shoot numbers out of some guys across the U.S., both returning and new.

With those kinds of numbers, it’s no surprise Ubisoft and Massive aren’t done with the series. Tom Clancy's The Division 3 is also officially in production at Massive Entertainment. Originally headed up by executive producer Julian Gerighty (who also led Star Wars Outlaws and The Division 2), The Division 3 is now in the hands of creative director Mathias Karlson, game director on The Division 2. Gerighty recently left Ubisoft to work at Battlefield developer DICE .

Gerighty confirmed his departure in a social media post just a week after appearing on a livestream to promote The Division 3 . “So, The Division 3 is in production, right?” he said before his departure. “This is not a secret. It's been announced. It's shaping up to be a monster.

“I can't really say anything more than that. But this is, within these walls in Massive, we are working extremely hard on something that I think will be as big an impact as Division 1 was.”

Tom Clancy’s The Division 2 Echoes of Central Park DLC Screenshots

Following his departure, Massive reassured fans that The Division 3 was in safe hands. “For our players, don’t worry, Agents,” the studio said in a social media post. “Our teams who built this world with Julian are still here, carrying it forward with an ambitious, unchanged commitment to the future.”

There’s no word on when The Division 3 will launch, but Ubisoft is making it a priority. Late last year, Massive Entertainment introduced what it called a "voluntary career transition program," as part of a move to focus on The Division franchise and its Snowdrop game engine.

articles.title: Everything We Saw at Nintendo Indie World Showcase October 2026, Including Witchbrook Release Date
articles.summary: Nintendo’s Indie World Showcase is over, and we’ve got a roundup of all the announcements right here.
articles.body:
Nintendo’s Indie World Showcase is over, and we’ve got a roundup of all the announcements right here!

Indie World Showcase kicked off with a big announcement: Chucklefish's Witchbrook finally has a release date! The hotly anticipated magical life sim is coming in to PC, Nintendo Switch 1 and 2, and Xbox on January 28, 2027. There's a new gameplay trailer, too. That's not all. Outside of Indie World Showcase, Chucklefish confirmed plans for a PlayStation 5 port.

Witchbrook invites players to enrol as a witch-in-training at Witchbrook College, in the bustling seaside town of Mossport. Attend classes and complete assignments in Alchemy, Astrology, Tarot, Rituals, and more as you expand your magical knowledge, study hard to pass exams, and unlock spells on your path to graduation. Between lessons, forge friendships and find romance among a colourful cast of characters, start your own witch business helping the local community, or spend your time taking it easy! Join a club, attend seasonal events, go birdwatching, bug-catching, fishing and more! Renovate your cosy woodland cottage and garden, and customise your witch. Additionally, all of this and more can be experienced with up to 4 players in online multiplayer!

Winds of Viridia, from Shark Jump, is due out early 2027, with a free demo available from the eShop today.

As a child awakened from a seed, set out to restore balance to the once-great civilization of Viridia in this seamless action-adventure experience. Run, slide, grapple and launch into the air while exploring hidden locations, finding relics and battling enemies alongside your mothbug companion. Set to an original soundtrack from award-winning composers Kevin Penkin and Christopher Larkin, Winds of Viridia launches for Nintendo Switch 2 in early 2027.

City of None is a new indie game coming from one of the co-creators of the much-loved Celeste. It's due out next year. Here's the official blurb from Nintendo:

City of None from Extremely OK Games and Noel & Liam Berry: Venture into a metropolis filled with strange spirits, wicked beasts and ferocious robots in City of None, a brand-new action and puzzle platforming adventure from one of the co-creators of Celeste. The city’s five sectors each have their own distinctive environments, playstyles and four-color palettes, with winding pathways, unique items and enemies to battle in fast, intuitive combat. Upgrade your equipment with rare resources and fight to reclaim the city’s future from its ravenous rulers. City of None launches for Nintendo Switch 2 and Nintendo Switch in 2027.

Sword of the Sea is coming to Nintendo Switch 2

Giant Squid's 2025 adventure video game Sword of the Sea is coming to Switch 2 on October 29.

Surf across waves of sand and glistening waters in this atmospheric adventure from the studio behind ABZÛ and The Pathless. Ride the magical Hoversword across deserts, glaciers and shimmering seas as you explore the mysterious Necropolis and set out to restore a lost ocean. Build speed, catch waves, perform tricks and uncover hidden paths as life gradually returns to the world around you. Sword of the Sea launches for Nintendo Switch 2 on Oct. 29.

The lead designer of Dead Cells has a new game, Tenjutsu, which is now confirmed for Nintendo Switch 2. Dead Cells designer Sébastien Benard’s fast-paced, full-blooded action roguelike is coming to Switch 2 alongside PC in 2027, and we've got a new gameplay trailer.

Set within the densely packed, neon-soaked streets of Kuroboro City, Tenjutsu follows former yakuza Ten as she attempts to rebuild her life after returning home from prison. Unbeknownst to her, Kuroboro’s underground crime bosses see Ten’s release as a threat to their power, and will stop at nothing to eliminate her.

Riyo Games and Balor Games’ turn-based RPG Threads of Time has a summer 2027 launch on Nintendo Switch, Nintendo Switch 2, PC via Steam, and Xbox Series X and S. The Switch versions were also revealed today during Nintendo’s Indie World showcase.

In this epic turn-based RPG, gather a party of heroes from different historical eras as you journey through time and expose a sinister plot that threatens the past, present and future. Featuring vibrant pixel-infused visuals, a deep, story-rich campaign and over 100 original songs, Threads of Time brings the magic of classic JRPGs to the modern era when it launches for Nintendo Switch 2 and Nintendo Switch in summer 2027.

Dumpster Gang from Curve Games and Coyote House Games is a chaotic online sandbox that charges players with solving puzzles and stealing everything they can carry as a trash panda. It's due out on Switch 2 next March.

Live your best raccoon life in this chaotic online co-op sandbox for up to four players. Scavenge dumpsters, steal junk, raid snacks and commit tiny, harmless crimes as you work together to complete ridiculous missions and avoid the relentless Exterminator. Return to your hideout to customize it with treasures scavenged from your nightly adventures. Joy-Con 2 mouse controls are supported, as is GameShare locally or online via GameChat. Dumpster Gang scurries onto Nintendo Switch 2 in March 2027.

Super Battle Golf lets up to eight players battle in chaotic golf games. It's due out on Switch 2 on March 25, 2027.

Gear up for chaos in this multiplayer golf showdown, where up to eight players race to finish each hole with the fewest strokes while using weapons, power-ups and other tricks to sabotage the competition. Compete across a variety of colorful courses, customize your golfer and battle in frantic matches where everyone plays at the same time online and across platforms.

semiwork's viral viral online co-op extraction horror game R.E.P.O. is coming to Nintendo Switch 2 in 2027. It launched on Steam in early access form last year and blew up.

Retrieve valuable items from the haunted remains of humanity in this online1 co-op horror game. Find and extract everything from fragile ceramics to heavy pianos using a physics-based grabbing tool. As you explore terrifying environments filled with deadly threats, teamwork is essential since careless mistakes can quickly turn a successful operation into a disaster. Each level is procedurally generated, so no two runs are the same. R.E.P.O. launches for Nintendo Switch 2 in 2027.

Haunted Paws from LazyFlock is a two-player cosy adventure where you play as a puppy. It's due out next May, with a free demo available on the eShop later today.

Two puppies, one haunted mansion and a missing human to rescue. In this two-player co-op adventure, create and customize your own pups and team up with a friend in local co-op, including via GameShare, or online. Explore mysterious locations, solve puzzles, meet strange characters and face spooky creatures as you follow the trail deeper into the mansion. Haunted Paws launches for Nintendo Switch 2 and Nintendo Switch in May 2027. A free demo will be available later today on Nintendo eShop.

A fox girl and her frog companion are stranded on a mysterious island shrouded in darkness in this 3D action-adventure inspired by Japanese folklore. Explore the island and kindle light within shrines to reveal new routes and uncover hidden secrets. But beware: malicious oni demons lurk in the shadows, and your light is limited. Evade danger in escape sequences and uncover a way forward through one long night beneath an autumn moon. Kitsune: The Journey of Adashino launches for Nintendo Switch 2 and Nintendo Switch in Spring 2027.

Continue the adventures of Beatrix LeBeau as she journeys to Rainbow Island, a mysterious land brimming with ancient technology, unknown natural resources and an avalanche of wiggling, jiggling new slimes to discover. Uncover the island’s secrets as you build, ranch and farm within a beautiful conservatory overlooking Beatrix’s colorful new home. Slime Rancher 2 launches for Nintendo Switch 2 in January 2027.

articles.title: Wildwood Is Getting a 4K Steelbook – Up for Preorder Now
articles.body:
When it comes to giving an animated movie a particular look and vibe, accept no substitute for stop-motion animation. That’s the method used in Laika Studios’ excellent new movie Wildwood. The film just hit theaters, but it’s already available to preorder in physical formats, including a 4K steelbook release ( see it on Amazon ).

Although the steelbook's art and design are not yet available, I'd grab it sooner than later if you're interested, because limited-edition steelbooks like this tend to sell out. Preorders are also live for other formats as well.

Wildwood - Limited-Edition Steelbook (4K UHD + Blu-ray)

4K Steelbook ($39.99) : Amazon | Gruv | Walmart

4K Standard ($36.99) : Amazon | Gruv | Walmart

Blu-ray ($27.99) : Amazon | Gruv | Walmart

Wildwood is not quite a children’s movie since it’s rated PG-13, but thanks to its fable-like quality, it appeals to a wide range of ages. It all kicks off when a child is abducted and whisked away into an enchanted forest. The boy's teenage sister Prue and her classmate Curtis then go off to find him.

The movie features a star-studded voice cast, including Carey Mulligan, Mahershala Ali, Jacob Tremblay, Awkwafina, Angela Bassett, Charlie Day, Jemaine Clement, Tom Waits ( Tom Waits! ), and many more.

In IGN’s Wildwood review , critic Tom Jorgensen wrote, “Wildwood is an arresting, exciting fantasy epic made all the more impressive by the fact that its fully realized and well-thought out world is handmade and hand-animated. The craft on display from Laika and director Travis Knight through this story of grief and growing up is commendable, and Wildwood’s massive sense of both scale and whimsy are constant joys.”

As yet, we don’t have details on what kinds of bonus materials will be included in the release. Nor do we know when it will come out – that depends on how well it does in theaters. All that info will be available in the future, and I'll update this article when it comes to light.

Laika is no stranger to stop-motion animation. It’s the studio that made the films Coraline, ParaNorman, The Boxtrolls, Kubo and the Two Strings, and Missing Link. Wildwood fits right in with those, imbuing real emotional weight and in the narrative thanks in part to the stop-motion characters’ expressiveness.

This is by no means the only movie coming for home release in the next few months. You can also preorder movies like Clayface and The Odyssey , as well as new 4K editions of classics like the original Die Hard trilogy . For a full picture of what's coming soon, check out our often-updated list of upcoming 4K UHD Blu-ray release dates .

articles.title: Oogie Boogie's Big Game Walkthrough - Disney Dreamlight Valley Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Oogie Boogie's Big Game is the final Quest in the Quest series required to unlock Oogie Boogie as a Villager in Disney Dreamlight Valley. This Quest
articles.body:
Oogie Boogie's Big Game is the final Quest in the Quest series required to unlock Oogie Boogie as a Villager in Disney Dreamlight Valley . This Quest initially released on October 28, 2026. To start it, you must complete all previous Oogie Boogie Quests , up through Let the Games Begin , and then wait for another letter from Oogie Boogie to show up in your Mailbox.

Important PSA for Unlocking Oogie Boogie

If you want to unlock Oogie Boogie in 2026, you MUST begin his first Quest, A Halloween Invasion , no later than November 4, 2026. Once you have begun the first Quest, the other five can be completed at any time once they have unlocked.

As long as you have STARTED A Halloween Invasion, you will be able to unlock Oogie Boogie, even if you finish up the Quest chain after November 4.

If you missed out on Oogie Boogie in 2026, he will return to the Valley in October 2027 !

Oogie Boogie's letter says that it is time to settle things once and for all, so head through the Mirror in Scrooge's Store to enter the trickster's lair one last time. Head up the stairs and talk to Oogie Boogie, who will be at the top of the left staircase waiting for you.

The Boogieman has set up your final show down - you will play a board game. If you win, he will join the Valley. If he wins, he will turn the Valley into a realm of nightmares. The game consists of traveling around the game board while answering questions.

Step on each tile and select "Interact" to have Oogie Boogie ask you a question. Red tiles are general trivia questions, blue tiles are questions that involve looking at pictures, and green tiles are questions about Oogie Boogie himself. Blue tiles will require you to pick up a Memory to see the picture you need to look at. There are a total of 11 Questions, and you must answer them all correctly to win the quiz.

While you must get every question correctly to win, Oogie Boogie is surprisingly nice - he will let you try again as many times as you want. If you want to leave to do something else or go look around the Valley for answers, you can select "I'm getting out of here" at any time. You can then restart from your current tile whenever you like. Your current tile will be marked with a black question mark token.

More detailed information and hints about each question are provided later in this guide, but if you just want to see the answers, they are listed below

Question: Where in the Valley can you find Dandelions?

Dandelions are bright yellow flowers . They are found in one of the first Biomes you will encounter when entering Dreamlight Valley

Question: How many purple stars are there?

Pick up the Memory to see the picture, which shows the inside of the Dream Castle with several purple stars floating around. You can also see the picture on a screen next to Oogie Boogie. The purple stars you need to count are on the left side of the image.

Question: What is my (Oogie Boogie's) favorite type of stew?

You made this stew for Oogie Boogie during one of his previous Quests, The Oogie Boogie Contract ! You had to use replacement ingredients like seaweed and bananas, because the things it was made out of aren't found in the Valley!

This tile starts out blue, indicating a picture question - but, when you interact with it, Oogie Boogie turns it green and asks another question about himself instead!

Question: What do I (Oogie Boogie) have for a tongue?

Oogie Boogie's body is made from bugs inside a burlap sack , but it's not JUST bugs. What creepy critter is long and skinny enough to work as a tongue - and scares children whenever Oogie Boogie opens his mouth?

Question: How many ponds do you have in the Peaceful Meadow?

There is a large pond on one side of the Peaceful Meadow , and multiple small ponds on the other side. Step away from the board and take a look at the Map if you need to count them again!

This is another picture question, so pick up the Memory to get a closer look at the picture (or look at it on the screen next to Oogie Boogie.) The eggs are in a carton in the center of the picture . There are no hidden eggs outside the carton.

Once again, Oogie Boogie changes the color of the tile - this time, from red to green.

Question: Who is my (Oogie Boogie's) archnemesis?

The answer is another Villager who lives in Dreamlight Valley. He's named after the kind of creature he resembles. Take a careful look at how the answers are spelled, as there are some "almost right" options!

Question: Where can you see me late at night, even if I'm nowhere near you?

If you're struggling with this question, rewatch the opening scene of The Nightmare Before Christmas, where the song "This is Halloween" is performed. Where does Oogie Boogie show up when he sings his lines during the song? It's somewhere where Oogie Boogie can easily keep an eye on all of Halloween Town !

Question: What does Scrooge wear on his head?

Scrooge isn't much of a sports fan, so it's probably not a baseball cap. He's quite the high-class gentleman , so what is the most dignified and fancy of the options you have?

Question: How many potions are on Merlin's desk?

Merlin's desk is quite cluttered, but most of the items, such as the books, are a distraction. The potions you need to count are all purple in color. There is not enough room on the desk for a large number of potions.

For the final question, you need to talk to Oogie Boogie directly, rather than interacting with a tile.

Question: Other than Jack, who else is a huge thorn in my side?

This is primarily a spelling question. Avoid the spelling you're used to - it's a trick! Remember that, in the film The Nightmare Before Christmas, to get the people of Halloween Town interested in Christmas, Jack needed to make Santa sound scarier than he actually is, by giving him a scary name.

Welcome Oogie Boogie to Dreamlight Valley

You've gotten all the questions right! Oogie Boogie is furious, but he's willing to uphold the deal he made. He will move into the Valley as soon as you put down a House for him.

Leave Oogie Boogie's Lair and return to Dreamlight Valley. The Lair will disappear when this Quest ends, so make sure you don't leave anything behind!

Using Furniture mode, place Oogie Boogie's House anywhere in the Valley. Interact with the Scrooge McDuck sign and pay the required amount of Star Coins to build the House. Star Coin prices vary depending on what order Villagers are unlocked in, with a maximum of 10,000 Star Coins for later Villagers.

Finally, take a photo with Oogie Boogie to welcome him to the Valley. Talk to him to learn that he's still planning all sorts of schemes, but is reluctantly happy to have joined the Valley at last!

articles.title: Tubi Hidden Horror Gems for Halloween 2026
articles.summary: We've done the digging for you and rounded up some of the best hidden horror gems you can stream on Tubi this Halloween 2026. Best of all? They're all completely free to watch.
articles.body:
HBO might have prestige horror shows like IT: Welcome to Derry, and Apple might be packed full of new horror movies to rent, but don't ignore Tubi. It's a haunted attic of scary movies, provided you're willing to do a little digging through its intimidatingly massive library. From underappreciated slashers and deeply unsettling psychological thrillers to the sort of gloriously unhinged genre oddities that make you wonder how they ever got made, there's plenty lurking within the streamer’s catalogue. So, in the spirit of spooky season, we've done the digging for you and rounded up some of the best hidden horror gems you can stream on Tubi this Halloween 2026. Best of all? They're all completely free to watch.

Three men walk into a creepy church. Not the start of a bad joke, but the premise of a slow-build, deeply unnerving little British movie involving the investigation of a reported miracle. At first, it seems like fairly standard found-footage fodder, but then a sheep is set on fire, the sound of a baby crying echoes through the church, and suddenly there's talk of old pagan rituals. Even then, there's no way you'll predict the ending, which I can still, unfortunately, vividly recall years after seeing it.

This documentary-style movie about one man's grandmother and the entity, Sator, that she speaks to is unsettling in the best way, and well worth a watch for that. What makes it even more compelling is the backstory behind it . Filmmaker Jordan Graham based the story around his own family history and a being called Sator that his real-life grandmother had spoken about throughout her life. That grandmother - June Peterson - who was suffering from dementia, appears in the movie, and her house was used as a location. Her condition meant that her lines were improvised, and it was through that process that Graham discovered his real family history had more in common with a horror movie than he had previously known, and his grandmother stopped being a cameo and became the movie's focus.

Two words: zombie horse. If that doesn't convince you to watch this 2009 movie that somehow fell into obscurity, I don't know what will. Before they were Magneto and Superman, Michael Fassbender and Henry Cavill starred in a truly wild Joel Schumacher (The Lost Boys) movie that manages to pack Nazis, Norse magic, and drinking blood like Gatorade into its plot. It's occasionally tense, surprisingly nasty, and takes such big swings you'll chuckle at the sheer audacity of it all. Even better, Fassbender and Cavill approach it with absolute seriousness, which only makes it more fun.

This French pregnancy horror film isn't for everyone; in fact, it isn't for most people, but leaving it off the list would be criminal. When I tell you that the interior the title refers to is a woman's womb, you can start to see why this might not be one for family movie night. It's essentially a battle between two women over a baby, the only snag being that the baby is currently very much inside one of them. Béatrice Dalle plays the antagonist with terrifying gusto, and if you don't cover your eyes at least once during this, you deserve some sort of medal. The events of the film also take place on Christmas Eve, so technically, it's a holiday movie.

Christmas is always an awkward time for dysfunctional families, but this British horror pic takes it to the next level when protagonist Nick, his parents, sister, brother-in-law, and grandfather end up trapped inside their home by an ominous black substance. A message broadcast through their television tells them they're contaminated, and as the television continues to direct their actions and share information about their supposed situation, things get way worse than an argument over who hogged all of the gravy.

Tubi's catalogue is constantly changing, but if you want to hold your own Halloween horror film festival this weekend, these movies are all currently available and well worth your time.

Rachel Weber is the Head of Editorial Development at IGN and an elder millennial. She's been a professional nerd since 2006 when she got her start on Official PlayStation Magazine in the UK, and has since worked for GamesIndustry.Biz, Rolling Stone and GamesRadar. She loves horror, horror movies, horror games, Red Dead Redemption 2, and her Love and Deepspace boyfriends.

articles.title: $15 watch party tickets hit $177 or more on resale sites ahead of Game 5
articles.summary: After a Game 4 loss, the Brewers announced details of a Game 5 watch party with tickets set to go on sale to the public at noon Wednesday, Oct. 25.
articles.body:
Tickets to the Milwaukee Brewers ' World Series Game 5 watch party at American Family Field were listed for $176 or more on multiple resale sites after they became available to season ticket holders at 10 a.m. Wednesday, Oct. 28.

After an excruciating Game 4 loss in extra innings, the Brewers announced details of a Game 5 watch party with tickets set to go on sale to the general public at noon Wednesday. The tickets cost $15 if they're bought from the Brewers' website , though parking costs extra: $15 for preferred or $10 for general.

But on resale sites, some tickets were already available for those willing to pay a premium. On Vivid Seats and Gametime, the cheapest ticket was listed for $177, while StubHub had tickets listed for $245 to $876 or more as of 11 a.m. Wednesday.

Faces in the Crowd: World Series Game 4 at American Family Field

The game is scheduled to start at 7 p.m., but parking lots will open at 4:30 p.m. and gates to the ballpark will open at 5 p.m.

The watch parties at American Family Field for Games 3 and 4 sold out in about 15 minutes, causing prices to soar on resale sites, where some tickets were listed for hundreds of dollars. The Brewers estimated that 31,000 fans attended each of those watch parties.

A Brewers win in Game 5 would mean the franchise's first-ever World Series title .

articles.title: Vampir Is a Dark, Brutal MMORPG Focused on Bloody Violence
articles.body:
The MMORPG genre has been woefully lacking in vampire representation, but into that void steps Netmarble’s Vampir. It first launched in South Korea in 2025 before recently expanding to the West, and it’s now available in the U.S. on PC, iOS, and Android.

This is a game that really leans into the full vampire experience. It’s defined by blood, horror, and sexuality with brutal combat in a dark fantasy setting. From the start of the game, you’ll be treated to some gruesome scenes that set the tone of the world, and that tone carries into gameplay. There are five character classes to choose from, and they’re all aggressive damage dealers that can use vampires’ signature blood-draining abilities to restore HP and gain temporary combat buffs.

All the classes dish out death in stylish fashion, but the way they do it is very different. Carnage can use a variety of firearms with rapid-fire attacks. Bloodstained is a berserker with added durability that can channel its bloodlust into a powerful sword. Viper uses poisons, curses, and summoned creatures to deal AoE damage and control the battlefield. Grim Reaper is a stealth assassin that uses teleportation and a scythe to land critical strikes. And Akasha is a melee class that specializes in pursuing enemies.

No matter which class you’re playing, you’ll feel the impact of your attacks. Battles are marked by dismemberment that leaves bloodstains in their wake. High-quality graphics add to the impact, with a level of fidelity that’s particularly impressive on mobile. The dark vibe and aesthetics are heightened by the use of lighting and shadows, and character models are detailed with nicely rendered skin textures.

Since different people play MMOs for different reasons, Vampir provides separate spaces for people who want to focus on progression or competition. If you prefer to level up your character and gather resources with relative ease, you can do that on individual servers with no issue. If you’re the competitive type, you can jump into Gehenna, an inter-server PvP battlefield that becomes available early in the game.

Gehenna is a dedicated combat zone that can pit you against players with server honor on the line. You can form clans to team up with other players and compete together. Bosses will appear at set times, and defeating them can earn rewards for you and honor for your server, as well as high-value rewards delivered to your Clan Vault. It’s also possible to physically block the routes of other players during these boss battles, allowing your clan to form battle lines and giving you strategic options to ensure victory.

Gehenna content is split into seasons, with server matchups reshuffled when each new season begins. This creates new rivalries and prevents a single clan from monopolizing competition for an extended period of time.

There are also cooperative challenges, like a defense mode where you need to work together to defend your clan’s emblem from relentless waves of attackers. Competitive content ranges from small skirmishes to large-scale battles, including the seasonal Clan War of Occupation and official tournaments. Clans that manage to come out on top of these massive competitions get the highest rewards the game can offer.

Outside of those rewards, you can get character upgrade resources through the in-game shop. You buy these with Diamonds, which you can earn through field gameplay without spending money, up to a weekly farming limit. Diamonds are also used for summons in Vampir’s gacha system, which adds a unique mechanic to the genre’s standard pity system.

With each summon that isn’t Legendary grade, you’re awarded Care Points and you get rewards at certain point thresholds. Lower-grade summon results award more Care Points, so Common awards you more than Uncommon, which rewards more than Rare. So if you get a string of Common summons, it actually speeds up your progress toward a Legendary pull.

Vampir is available now on PC, iOS, and Android, and there’s a special launch reward event happening now where you can get a Designated Heroic Mount Summon Ticket, 100 million Gold, and a full set of Rare Equipment as soon as you start the game. Through gameplay, you can also earn Heroic Equipment and 1,100 summon chances. To keep up with the latest updates, you can follow the game YouTube , Facebook , and Discord .

articles.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Patch Makes It Impossible to Get a Nuke in Free-for-All
articles.summary: A new patch for Modern Warfare 4 has players up in arms because it prevents you from getting a tactical nuke Killstreak in Free-for-All, one of the Multiplayer modes.
articles.body:
A new patch for Modern Warfare 4 has players up in arms because it prevents you from getting a tactical nuke Killstreak in Free-for-All, one of the Multiplayer modes.

“We've made two adjustments to Free-for-All in #MW4,” developer Infinity Ward announced in a tweet , which included confirmation of a score reduction and a party size change. Now, you can only enter Free-For-All matches with one friend in your party. On top of that, the score required to win a Free-For-All match has been reduced to 25 kills. It was previously 30 kills.

Players are upset because this change locks them out of 100% completing the game. A Calling Card called Ground Zero requires players to earn a tactical nuke in a Free-For-All match, but the new score cap prevents this from being possible, since you need to earn 30 consecutive kills without dying to get a nuke.

Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Classic Prestige Rewards

There’s no word on whether Activision and Infinity Ward plan to reduce the requirement for a nuke in Free-For-All or change the Calling Card to something that’s, you know, possible.

These changes come to the game after an uptick in account boosting in Free-For-All. Players who wanted to earn the Ground Zero Calling Card were coming in with three friends and farming each other to earn the nuke, essentially ruining the game for everyone else.

Obviously, these changes should put an end to that, but it’s annoying for players who wanted to play Free-For-All legitimately with their friends, or earn the Calling Card the right way. “One of the calling cards is literally 30kills in a FFA match lmao brain dead,” said one player . “Can we not keep changing stuff? FFA has always been 30 kills why change it now?” asked another .

Sentiment is almost entirely negative in the replies to the announcement so it won’t be a huge surprise if Infinity Ward reverses the decision or at least tweaks it in some way. This news landed just after Shipment, one of Call of Duty’s most iconic maps, was added to Modern Warfare 4 .

PlayStation is bringing back the '90s transparent trend with the Prism Collection, a spread of DualSense controllers and matching PS5 covers in three new colorways.

Preorders open on November 10 at 10am local time ahead of the collection's full launch next year. The Prism Collection DualSense controllers, available in Flare Orange, Emerald Green, and Graphite Gray, are releasing globally with a recommended retail price (RRP) of $84.99 USD (€84.99/£74.99). Matching PS5 console covers have an RRP of $74.99 USD (€74.99/£64.99).

A PlayStation blog post offers a closer look at the new see-through designs. The images are accompanied by insights from the design team, who were particularly “excited to bring a transparent appearance to PS5.”

PlayStation Prism Collection DualSense Controllers

"We wanted to bring back the iconic see-through trend of the late '90s in a fresh, modern way that complements the PS5’s industrial design," said PlayStation designer Leo Cardoso. The blog post also highlights that the see-through casing offers a “closer look at the design and craftsmanship behind our DualSense controllers and PlayStation 5 consoles.”

Fellow designer Satoshi Aoyagi describes the three colors the team chose to showcase the transparent mould: “A vibrant orange that subtly takes on a rosy hue where the transparent material overlaps, a deep hunter green that gains depth through its transparency, and a cool-toned storm gray.”

The full Prism Collection will be available to preorder from PlayStation Direct and select retailers starting November 10, with the full release scheduled for February 4.

Sony has released over a dozen DualSense color variants in the PS5 generation on top of limited-edition controllers tied to specific game releases like Astro Bot and Death Stranding .

While the company is expanding the reach of its hardware collaborations, like a new DualSense controller with Kpop star Lisa , its most popular release of late was the 30th Anniversary PlayStation collection . With the Prism Collection, the design team appears to be doubling down on audience demand for retro designs that tap into nostalgia for classic gaming eras.

PlayStation as a whole continues to be embroiled in controversies stemming from Sony's decision to cut disc production as well as a number of studio closures . Despite the backlash, Sony saw a 22% increase in PS5 sales during the past month, likely tied to the release of Insomniac’s Wolverine and the lead-up to GTA 6.

articles.title: Where to Find Rock Salt - Best Loot Locations - Arc Raiders Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Rock Salt is a resource that you can find while playing ARC Raiders. It's a crucial component for the Soul's Offering research, available for a
articles.body:
Rock Salt is a resource that you can find while playing ARC Raiders . It's a crucial component for the Soul's Offering research, available for a limited time. You'll need it to complete the first page of this project, and tracking it down can be difficult. There are a few places you can focus on to help narrow down your search. Here's everything you need to know about where to find Rock Salt while playing ARC Raiders.

Rock Salt is a lootable material that regularly appears in Residential loot tables as a trinket. When I went to search for it, I was able to find it in the Grandioso Apartments, in a kitchen drawer.

Many other players have also discovered it throughout their playing by searching in Residential looting areas. Each map contains areas with Residential looting locations, but the best ones are going to be the Buried City , Dam Battlegrounds , or The Blue Gate .

For the Buried City, you want to stick to the southern part of the map, so you can sweep through the Grandioso Apartments, to the Santa Maria Houses, partially through Plaza Rosa, and finish up with Old Town on the east side. All of these locations are close to residential areas, ideal for tracking down Rock Salt.

If you want to go to the Dam Battlegrounds, you'll want to stick to the north and northwest sides of the map. Here, you'll find the Pale Apartments, the Ruby Residents, and the Pattern House next to the lower Generation Complex. These are all ideal locations to search through old resident homes to potentially find Rock Salt.

Finally, for The Blue Gate, you'll want to search through the Village and the Raider's Refuge on the north side. The Village has the most concentration of houses in the region, making it the best location to try and find Rock Salt. Alternatively, you can head south and search through the Ruined Homestead and the Olive Grove for this item.

Those are the three locations you'll want to focus on, but there's a chance to find it across any Residential loot location in ARC Raiders. You do want to avoid Spaceport, as it doesn't have any, and there's a slim chance of finding; still possible, though!

articles.title: Wendy's Is Making a Turn-Based RPG and It Actually Looks Really Good
articles.summary: Wendy’s — yes, the American fast food chain — is releasing a surprisingly gorgeous, pixelated, turn-based RPG on Steam, and the internet is legitimately stunned by how good it looks.
articles.body:
Wendy’s — yes, the American fast food chain — is releasing a surprisingly gorgeous, pixelated, turn-based RPG on Steam, and the internet is legitimately stunned by how good it looks.

The game, titled WendyQuest: Legend of the Four Corner Stones, is a 2D RPG where players join Wendy in her journey to “battle evil mech-monsters to save a culinary kingdom in peril.”

A trailer and screenshots for the game show Wendy and a party of three other adventurers traversing terrain fraught with food-themed obstacles and duking it out with sentient menu items. For instance, one of the enemies Wendy faces is a container full of french fries that have transformed into snake-like monsters called ‘Frydusa.’ In one gameplay still, she must find a way around a river of sauce that has spilled out from a container.

WendyQuest: Legend of the Four Corner Stones Screenshots

The game’s dialogue seems to poke fun at itself, with Wendy saying in one screenshot, “Looks like he’s been writing notes to some guy named Baconator. No way that’s a real name.” In another, she asks, “Where’s the beef?”

Of course, Wendy can use a Dave’s Single, Junior Bacon Cheeseburger, and other menu items to restore her HP during battle, where she’s joined by allies like Sir Chicken and more.

The game is set to release “soon,” with no specific launch date given. It does have an official Steam page , suggesting that this isn’t just a gimmick game but an actual, fully-fledged title with real effort and intent behind it.

WendyQuest is developed by 81monkeys, an independent game studio based out of Port Moody, British Columbia. They are also working on a game called World of Anterra, which is described as “an innovative open world roleplaying game” inspired by “classic and modern” titles.

Thus far, reactions to Wendy’s pixelated project have been largely positive. “GOTY contender. This actually looks great,” one user joked on Twitter/X.

“Wait, why does it look kind of good?” another asked .

“I honestly miss fast food games....Excited to play this!” said another .

Still others are pleased that no AI was used in this game’s production, despite it being, for all intents and purposes, a marketing tactic. Its Steam page proudly states that the title is “100% fresh and 100% human made.”

Of course, others couldn’t help but compare it to Burger King’s infamous Sneak King game from ages long past (2006), where players could “step into the King’s royal shoes and use cunning stealth to sneak up behind unsuspecting people and bestow them with a delicious meal.” (While a novelty, it wasn't an especially 'good' game. We rated it a 6.7 out of 10 .)

This isn't the first time Wendy's has made a game; in fact, it released a free, 100-page tabletop RPG back in 2019 called Feast of Legends where players could battle Ronald McDonald. I have to admit that the chain's latest game is one of the more ambitious fast food marketing tactics I’ve seen thus far, and oddly, I’m actually keen on playing it when it actually comes out. Dangit — now I’m craving a Frosty.

articles.title: Football Fans Share Their Visceral Reactions to Nicolas Cage’s John Madden: ‘A Disgraceful Portrayal of a Great Man’
articles.summary: NFL fans expressed some pretty heated responses on social media to the first clip of Nicolas Cage in the upcoming movie Madden, where the Oscar winner portrays the legendary football TV commentator John Madden.
articles.body:
NFL fans expressed some pretty heated responses on social media to the first clip of Nicolas Cage in the upcoming movie Madden , where the Oscar winner portrays the legendary football TV commentator John Madden.

Director David O. Russell’s film chronicles Madden’s relationship with Al Davis (played by Christian Bale) and Madden’s journey, as the official synopsis puts it, "from a Super Bowl-winning partnership with the Raiders, to becoming football’s most recognizable voice, to building the worldwide Madden NFL video game."

In the clip (seen below), Cage’s Madden sits opposite ​​Joel Murray’s Pat Summerall as Madden breaks down a play on the telestrator while the crew in the booth react to it.

And football commentary was never the same. #MaddenMovie. November 18. — Prime Movies (@primemovies) October 27, 2026

And football commentary was never the same. #MaddenMovie. November 18.

Judging by the visceral responses from a slew of football fans on social media , they appear to be mostly upset that Cage doesn’t sound like the iconic sports host. (I guess these fans must have missed the film’s trailer, since this isn’t the first time Cage’s Madden performance has been revealed.)

Here's a sample of the kinds of responses that have been posted:

“This is a disgraceful portrayal of a great man.” – AFL Godfather

“What a nightmare. Madden was a Legendary coach - capital Legendary - and this is what they come up with?” – tonmile trader

“Sigh....this could have been so good. I can't not hear Cage's voice. Or not see Cage's face. This is an insulting caricature of John Madden. I don't know how this got made.” – Matthew Ross

“Nicolas Cage told the director of the new Madden movie that John Madden's voice 'may not be anatomically possible/ for him to do. They went ahead and made the whole movie anyway.” – Aakash Gupta

“I was wondering how Nicolas Cage was going to pull off being Madden. Turns out he didn’t pull it off at all.” – Brian O’Leary

“I mean this is basically a desecration of Madden’s legacy. Astoundingly bad.” – Mark Valorian

“He sounds like 10% Jimmy Stewart, 90% Nicolas Cage. 0% Madden.” – Edward Fear

“Everyone is rightfully dogpiling on Nicolas Cage as Madden here, but the Pat Summerall is even more disrespectful. Looks and sounds nothing like Pat, acts annoyed by Madden, seems to have no football knowledge of his own. This movie needs to be shelved.” – Tim Roberts

“There are going to have to be arrests. Accountability for this is a must.” – Rob Slater

Criticisms weren’t reserved just for the performances. Cinema Tweets blasted the man behind the camera in their post, saying, “David O. Russell might never direct a film again after Madden. Do I want that to happen? Of course not. I want Madden to be a huge success. But if this film turns out as bad as it looks (and based on this trailer…it looks bad), who would ever bankroll O. Russell again? He just made the worst film of his career with Amsterdam & if he follows it up with another flop, why would anyone take another chance on him? Especially when you consider how difficult he is to work with as a director. There’s a lot on the line for O. Russell right now.”

In addition to Cage and Bale, Madden also stars Kathryn Hahn, Sienna Miller, John Mulaney, and Shane Gillis. Madden opens in select theaters on November 18, 2026 via Amazon MGM Studios.

articles.title: 'Appreciate the Fans' — GTA 5 Cast Tell Jason and Lucia’s Actors the Most Important Things They Should Know Before GTA 6 Launches Them to Fame
articles.summary: The stars behind GTA 5’s Franklin, Michael, and Trevor, along with the voice of CJ from San Andreas, were asked if they had any advice for the actors playing GTA 6’s Jason and Lucia now that the game is almost here.
articles.body:
The stars behind GTA 5’s Franklin, Michael, and Trevor, along with the voice of CJ from San Andreas, were asked if they had any advice for the actors playing GTA 6’s Jason and Lucia now that the game is almost here.

The long wait for GTA 6 is almost over. After 13 years, the game is finally set to release on November 19 in one of the biggest (and potentially most expensive) pop culture moments in history.

Knowing just how passionate Rockstar’s fanbase can be, actors who starred in previous games in the franchise shared their words of wisdom with the as-yet unannounced actors who are playing Jason and Lucia, the dual protagonists of GTA 6, in an interview with All Out Gaming at MCM Comic Con.

“Have fun,” CJ’s actor, Young Maylay, said.

“To be honest, just listen to what Rockstar says,” Shawn ‘Solo’ Fonteno, famous for playing Franklin in GTA 5, added. “They’re gonna lead you in the right direction. … But get ready. That’s all I can say, is get ready. It’s a ride that they’re gonna be on for a while.”

Young Maylay continued, remarking on how the GTA games have garnered dedicated fanbases from multiple generations of players. “We’ll always be the characters that we are, and for the generation of kids who are coming up, you’re gonna have certain brackets,” he said.

“Right now, I got all the OGs. Everybody coming in my line — you catch some youngsters, but you got guys with the grey hair coming in saying, ‘Hey man! You’re the guy, CJ!’ And they [gesturing to the GTA 5 cast] have all the youngsters right now. So, during this time period, you’re gonna grow with your fanbase. It’s not like everything’s gonna get shut down by you guys [speaking of GTA 6]… we’ll always be those characters, and you can’t take that from us.”

Ned Luke, who played Michael De Santa in GTA 5 , urged the upcoming stars to be grateful for the game’s fans. “Just make sure that you appreciate the fans. Let the fans know… fake appreciation, they can smell it. You have to really appreciate them, genuinely, because what we have is because of them. If you don’t have the fans, you don’t got nothin’. They’re the game, and that’s the bottom line,” he imparted.

The cast's warm sentiments toward GTA fans is at odds with one particular star in the franchise: Steven Ogg, who infamously said he felt "nothing inside" regarding GTA 6 because he's "not a gamer" and has "never played a video game" before. That being said, he did suggest killing off his character at the beginning of GTA 6 as a means of "passing the torch" to the next era. "I think that would be cool, because it also acknowledges the fans of like, 'Hey, thank you.' Pass the torch, stomp Trevor's head in, and sort of put an end to that and allow a new generation to take over," he mused back in 2025.

Thus far, the actors who play Jason and Lucia have not been officially announced, though fans are extremely convinced that they’ve discovered the gal who lent her facial features to Jason’s partner in crime. Fans suspect she will be played by an actress named Manni L. Perez , as she has the exact same voice and bears a strong resemblance with the GTA protagonist. (For her part, she’s been very careful to honor her supposed NDA, if she really is involved in the project.)

The fervor around GTA 6 is at an all-time high. Rockstar is ramping up marketing for the title in a major way with a Vice City-themed takeover of Miami that includes massive signs advertising the fictional city, even partnering with the Miami Heat to give the team some Vice City uniforms for their November 18 game against the Milwaukee Bucks. Players will even get a chance to eat at one of the game’s fast food joints , Burger Shot, at the Kaseya Center while they watch the two teams face off on the court.

articles.title: Where to Find Dead Flowers - Best Loot Locations - Arc Raiders Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Dead Flowers are a resource that you'll need to collect in ARC Raiders for the Soul's Offering limited-time event. It's a hard-to-find Uncommon
articles.body:
Dead Flowers are a resource that you'll need to collect in ARC Raiders for the Soul's Offering limited-time event. It's a hard-to-find Uncommon item that won't show up everywhere, making it a difficult one to narrow down. In this guide, we'll be providing you with the best locations where you can find Dead Flowers throughout your time playing ARC Raiders to complete these tasks in the limited event.

Dead Flowers are an uncommon trinket, similar to the other required for this event, Rock Salt . However, Dead Flowers are available in the Old World, Residential, and Commercial looting districts. You have a few more options available to you for looting opportunities, but that doesn't quite make it easier, as you might be trying to cast a wider net.

You can find Old World, Residential, and Commercial looting areas littered throughout each of the maps. The best locations to find Dead Flowers are going to be on the Buried City , The Blue Gate , Dam Battlegrounds , and Pendola Pass, maps.

For Buried City, you want to sweep the southern section and go through the Grandioso Apartments, Plaza Rosa, and the Santa Maria Houses. These are all Residential and Commercial districts that offer a chance for you to get Dead Flowers from the various containers within them. You can also investigate the north, looking through the Space Travel and Library buildings.

When it comes to searching for Dead Flowers in Dam Battlegrounds, you primarily want to stick to the northern apartments. You'll go through the Pale Apartments, Ruby Resident, and Pattern House. However, you can also pivot to the center of the map and look through the Research & Administration building or the Testing Annex, which is close to an extraction gate.

For those who prefer The Blue Gate, you'll want to stick to the Village in the far north. That's the best place to find Dead Flowers throughout the many houses in that area. However, you can try your luck by also searching through the Ruined Homestead, the Olive Grove, or the Ancient Fort to the south. It all depends on where you spawn during your match.

Finally, you can try Pendola Pass. There, you'll want to stick to the central points of interest of that location, searching through the Commissary Supermarket, Almatera Station, or Old Town. Some players have also gotten lucky by searching the containers and homes directly under the Fallen Emperor, but this might be moderately risky.

Those are the primary regions I recommend searching for Dead Flowers. However, any map with Commercial, Residential, or Old World looting areas has a chance for you to find Dead Flowers, adding it to your portion of the Soul's Offering event.

articles.title: James Gunn Confirms Batman and Wonder Woman Are 'Diamond Characters' in the DCU Despite Their Continued Absence
articles.summary: James Gunn has clarified DC Studios’ 8-10 year roadmap and confirmed its focus on Superman, Batman, and Wonder Woman as its “diamond characters.”
articles.body:
James Gunn has clarified DC Studios’ 8-10 year roadmap and confirmed its focus on Superman, Batman, and Wonder Woman as its “diamond characters.”

Gunn shared this information on Threads in response to a now-deleted post, where he urged the original poster to study up on his quotes from January 2023 in regards to what his version of the DCU will end up looking like.

“I said some stories would be standalone like the Guardians movies were (which is what Clayface is), and some stories would have part of a larger narrative structure, which is what the Superman Saga is. All that said, each piece of the larger story should work on its own with or without having to see everything else,” he said.

He went on to clarify that the “often-cited 8-10 year roadmap” for the DCU doesn’t just apply to story points, but also outlines the plan for “DC as a whole.” This includes focusing on “diamond characters,” which Gunn confirmed are, perhaps unsurprisingly, Superman, Batman, and Wonder Woman, as well as “smaller characters we could turn into diamonds.” These smaller characters were listed as Krypto the Superdog, John Stewart, and Peacemaker.

According to Gunn, this plan also factors in how DC will “foster filmmaker freedom and allow for multiple tones and ratings, the influences of Star Wars and George R.R. Martin, and so much more."

“It's exciting seeing things start to come together, and all that makes me even more excited for what we have in store for everyone in Man of Tomorrow,” he said.

It’s encouraging to see Gunn confirm that Batman and Wonder Woman are still a big focus for his DCU, given that we haven’t seen hide nor hair of Wonder Woman and barely a glimpse of Batman’s silhouette in the animated Creature Commandos series.

Thus far, the only “diamond character” mentioned in this specific post that has been featured in Gunn’s DCU is Superman. Elsewhere, the Lanterns and Clayface have finally gotten some love (with Lanterns receiving rave reviews , though audience opinions on Clayface have been a mixed bag ), and The People v. Gorilla Grodd is also in the works. It seems that Supergirl wasn’t mentioned as either a “diamond character” or a character that could be turned "into a diamond" in Gunn's post — though, given that she had her own movie, it’s safe to assume that she has firmly established her place in the DCU hierarchy as a central figure.

Batman is another story altogether. Unrelated to Matt Reeves’ The Batman movies, the DCU’s take on the caped crusader has yet to be revealed; while Alan Ritchson was a popular pick from fans, DC Studios boss Peter Safran has stated they still haven’t found the right role for him to play. Batman is set to have his own movie in the DCU, titled The Brave and the Bold , which is in the works but has no official release date.

Where Wonder Woman fits in Gunn’s DCU is just as nebulous. Similarly, no casting has been confirmed for this part, though fans are convinced that Adria Arjona will soon wield the Lasso of Truth on screen. It’s also unclear when, or how, she’ll be introduced to things, but Gunn has made it clear that she’s a priority.

In other exciting DC news, a live-action Poison Ivy show was confirmed to be in the works earlier this month, with The Penguin showrunner Lauren LeFranc set to produce. Similarly, no casting has been confirmed (though rumors of ScarJo playing the character continue to swirl).
